question.text: 1 L closed flask contains a mixture of 4 g of methane and 4.4 g of carbon dioxide. The pressure inside the flask at $27^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ is [Assume ideal behaviour of gases]

solution.text:
no. of moles of $\mathrm{CH}_4\left(\mathrm{n}_1\right)=\frac{4}{16}=0.25 \mathrm{~mol}$
no. of moles of $\mathrm{CO}_2\left(\mathrm{n}_2\right)=\frac{4.4}{44}=0.1 \mathrm{~mol}$
Total no. of moles $\left(\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{T}}\right)=\mathrm{n}_1+\mathrm{n}_2=0.35 \mathrm{~mol}$
$\therefore \quad P=\frac{0.35 \times 0.082 \times 300}{1}=8.6 \mathrm{~atm}$

question.text: On electrolysis of water, a total of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mole</mi></math> of gases is evolved. The amount of water decomposed is

solution.text:
∵ Only one mole of total gases are evolved and H2O decomposes as

H2O→decompositionH2+12O2

i.e. total moles =1+12=32 moles by one mole of H2O

Now,

∵ 32 moles of gases are evolved by =1 mole of H2O

∴ 1 mole of gases are evolved by =13/2=23

Hence, 1 mole of total gases are evolved by 23 mole of H2O.

$$

question.text: An ideal gaseous mixture of ethane $\left(\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{6}\right)$ and ethene $\left(\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{4}\right)$ occupies 28 litre at 1 atm and $273 \mathrm{~K}$. The mixture reacts completely with $128 \mathrm{~g}$ $\mathrm{O}_{2}$ to produce $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O} .$ Mole fraction at $\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{6}$ in the mixture is:

solution.text:
$\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{6}+3.5 \mathrm{O}_{2} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{CO}_{2}+3 \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O} ;$

$\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{4}+3 \mathrm{O}_{2} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{CO}_{2}+2 \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}$

Let volume of ethane is $\mathrm{x}$ litre, $22.4 \times 4=3.5 \mathrm{x}+3(28-\mathrm{x})$

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=11.2$ litre

at constant $\mathrm{T}$ and $\mathrm{P}, \mathrm{V} \propto \mathrm{n} ;$

$\Rightarrow$ Mole fraction of $\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{6}$ in mixture $=\frac{11.2}{28}=0.4$

question.text: Equal weights of $\mathrm{NaCl}$ and $\mathrm{KCl}$ are dissolved separately in equal volumes of solutions. Molarity of the two solutions will be :

options.text: That of $\mathrm{NaCl}$ will be less than that of $\mathrm{KCl}$
That of $\mathrm{NaCl}$ will be more than that of $\mathrm{KCl}$ solution
That of $\mathrm{NaCl}$ will be about half of that of $\mathrm{KCl}$ solution

solution.text: When equal weights of different solutes are present in equal volumes of solution the molarity is inversely related to molecular mass of the solute. Mol. mass of $\mathrm{NaCl}$ is less than $\mathrm{KCl}$. Hence, molarity of $\mathrm{NaCl}$ solution will be more.
